A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the downscaling model based on point scale soil thermal inertia relationship is a more robust and reliable approach to downscale coarse spatial resolution satellite derived soil moisture retrievals, compared to the downscaling model built based on GLDAS land surface model outputs.

, the downscaling model built using point scale in situ soil moisture data produced more accurate downscaled soil moisture retrievals than the model built using the 25 km GLDAS data, especially in the regions with low thermal inertia values.

the downscaling models built by using in situ point scale soil temperature and soil moisture data produced better downscaled soil moisture retrievals than the model built using GLDAS land surface model outputs, over semi arid region.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the model built at 25 km resolution is more robust and can be easily implemented in large areas, whereas the model built at point scale requires a large number of in situ soil moisture data points, which are not always available.
the soil thermal inertia downscaling approach can be used to downscale coarse spatial resolution satellite derived soil moisture retrievals into higher resolution.
, the soil thermal inertia based approach can be used for downscaling coarse spatial resolution soil moisture products into finer resolutions.
